subject: Life Skills
title: Why Passwords Get Cracked
description: A quick, practical guide to Why Passwords Get Cracked.

hook.text: The most common password in the world is still '123456.' Millions of people use it right now.

buildup.text: Hackers don't guess your password manually. Software tries billions of combos per second.

discovery.text: Length beats complexity. A 16-character passphrase is harder to crack than an 8-character jumble.

twist.text: Adding one capital and a symbol feels secure but barely slows a modern cracking rig down.

climax.text: String four random words together. 'Correct horse battery staple' is both memorable and tough.

punchline.text: Longer beats cleverer. Four silly words win.

quiz.question: What makes a password hardest to crack?
options: Making it longer with random words
